subject: tu:game/sfx/sfx
value: "A defake_gate BASELINE ALREADY EXISTS, DO NOT RE-BASELINE" IS NOT A PORTABLE INSTRUCTION ACROSS RUNS: the baseline lives at `build/GUNE5D/gate/<unit>.json`, which is a GITIGNORED BUILD ARTEFACT inside the worktree that took it. When that worktree is removed after integration, the baseline is destroyed with it, and a fresh worktree's `defake_gate.py check` exits 2 with `no baseline at build\GUNE5D\gate\<unit>.json`. MEASURED this run: a work order forbade re-baselining game/sfx/sfx on the grounds that run 26 had one; a filesystem-wide search for `game_sfx_sfx.json` across every registered worktree returned NOTHING, because run 26's worktree had been pruned. THE PREMISE WAS REFUTED, not merely stale. THE CORRECT RECOVERY -- and the reason the prohibition existed is still sound -- is to rebuild the baseline FROM A CLEAN HEAD TREE, never from your edited tree: save your working file to scratch, write the `git show HEAD:<path>` bytes over it (python `write_bytes`, not a PowerShell redirect, per the BOM trap), run `defake_gate.py baseline <unit>`, then restore your edit. That reconstructs the identical reference the prior run banked, because HEAD IS the prior run's merged result -- and it is verifiable: the reconstructed baseline printed `72 functions (53 at real 0)`, character-for-character the figure the run-26 attempt record had written down. Taking the baseline from an EDITED tree is the actual laundering hazard the prohibition was aimed at, and it is what the naive `defake_gate.py baseline` call would have done. GENERAL RULE: an instruction of the form "artefact X exists from run N, reuse it" must name the artefact's PATH and its lifetime; if the path is under `build/`, treat the artefact as absent and state the reconstruction procedure instead. Cross-check the reconstruction against a figure the prior record quoted -- that check is free and converts a trust assumption into a measurement.
